chunks: As for what was narrated by Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from ʿAlī ibn Saʿīd, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the grave-robber. He said: “If grave-digging is not his habit, his hand is not cut off, but he is disciplined.”

key_terms.النَّبَّاشِ: the grave-robber; one who exhumes graves unlawfully
key_terms.لَمْ يُقْطَعْ: the hadd punishment of amputation is not carried out
key_terms.يُعَزَّرُ: he is given discretionary disciplinary punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a grave-robber in Shia hadith if grave-digging is not his habit?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the grave-robber (nabbāsh). Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that if exhuming graves is not a habitual practice for the offender, the fixed punishment of amputation is not applied, and instead he is subject to taʿzīr discretionary discipline.
